findings.title: Malformed timestamp meanings crash SignalEvent validation
findings.description: `SignalEvent.__post_init__` rejects a non-`AVAILABLE_AT` meaning by formatting `self.time.meaning.value` at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/signals.py:76-80`. However, `Timestamp` does not validate `meaning` at runtime: the field is only annotated at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/timestamps.py:54-55`, `__post_init__` only calls `require_int64_ns` at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/timestamps.py:57-58`, and `require_int64_ns` only checks the numeric range at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/timestamps.py:61-64`. A value such as `Timestamp(100, "event_time")` can therefore reach `SignalEvent`; because a plain string has no `.value`, validation raises `AttributeError` instead of the typed `InvalidSignalError` used by the surrounding checks at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/signals.py:64-75`. Validate `self.time.meaning` before reading `.value`, or construct the error without assuming it is a `TimeMeaning`.

findings.title: Missing regression test for malformed timestamp meanings
findings.description: The `test_event_rejects` parametrization at `tests/core_model/test_signals.py:79-94` covers integer times, alternate `TimeMeaning` enum members, float `ns`, bad instrument ids, plain-string action/direction values, and bad confidences, but it has no case where `Timestamp.meaning` is a plain string or other non-`TimeMeaning` object. Since `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/timestamps.py:54-58` does not enforce the meaning type and `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/signals.py:76-80` dereferences `.value`, this omission leaves the above crash path untested. Add a parametrized negative case asserting `InvalidSignalError` for malformed meanings.
